newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Governor OKs licence exemption on phones.
newsitem.headline: HK Governor OKs licence exemption on phones.

text.p: Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten has approved the making of an exemption order to permit the sale and use of new types of cordless telephones and cordless data communications equipment without the need to obtain a licence, the government said in statement on Thursday.

The order will cover equipment conforming to the Japanese Personal Handy-Phone System (PHS) and the European Digital Enhanced Cordless Telecommunications (DECT) technical standards, and certain types of cordless telephones conforming to American standards, it said.
The previous exemption order only covers existing types of cordless telephones conforming to the CT-0 and the CT-2 standards.

Although the PHS and DECT technologies may be used for public mobile services called Cordless Access Service, the new exemption order will cover the use of the equipment for private communications only, the statement said.
Suppliers and dealers can sell only equipment that has been type-approved by the Office of the Telecommunications Authority, it said.
